agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Diffusion stage, mechanisms and bounded timing implications

analytical_question: How far have dynamically tool-selecting language-model agents, specifically chart-to-approved-source reconciliation, diffused; what mechanisms matter for this hypothetical financial firm and what bounded timing follows?
general_et_finding: INNOVATION: A language-model agent dynamically chooses tools and reacts to tool observations during a bounded multi-step task. This is not synonymous with all AI, conversational generative AI, licensed tools or deterministic automation. ONLY C1 and S2 are supplied. C1 outlines Rogers innovators, early adopters, early majority, late majority and laggards, the bell-shaped incidence of new adopters versus the cumulative S-curve, and conceptual 2.5%, 13.5% and 16% illustrations. These positions require a defined social system and eligible denominator. S2 documents US businesses' any-AI use during the period ending May 3 2026: Finance and Insurance 33.9%, compared with 19.8% nationally. Its BTOS data span December 14 2025–May 3 2026; the current-use question concerns the previous two weeks, and wording expanded in November 2025. Released May 26 and checked October 22, the statistic remains a dated broad-AI result, not a current agentic deployment rate or an October estimate. No agent-specific evidence is in this packet. GENERAL AGENT DIFFUSION UNDETERMINED; CHASM UNDETERMINED. No time series or eventual adopter population exists for fitting an S-curve or Bass forecast; lack of evidence does not mean zero adoption.
application_finding: APPLICATION DIFFUSION UNDETERMINED: C1 is theory, and S2 measures broadly defined AI use by US businesses, not chart reconciliation with a tool-selecting agent; no defensible adoption numerator or peer denominator exists. Five factors for chart-to-source review: (1) Relative advantage—reduced review effort or improved error detection is a hypothesis, with no comparative time, accuracy, false-correction, human-checking or total-cost observations versus manual and deterministic checks (case assumptions/inference). (2) Compatibility—read-only approved tables and human report accountability offer potential process fit, but access to sensitive production tables/models is not approved (case facts/inference). (3) Complexity—permissions, multistep consistency, analyst expertise and audit trails plausibly constrain use; C1 supplies the framework, not a measured technical effect. (4) Trialability—an approved isolated synthetic/public-only sandbox permits reversible testing in principle, not proof of production transfer or an executed trial (case premise). (5) Observability—reviewable discrepancy logs and independently verified peer outcomes would permit assessment, but none has been observed; merely being able to design a log does not merit a high empirical rating. Most consequential inhibitor: lack of observed comparative advantage/credible application-peer evidence (interpretation), interacting with access restrictions and operational complexity. S2 cannot diagnose the factor effects for agents. Chart-review penetration, financial-peer Rogers stage and chasm crossing are withheld.

evidence.claim: At the period ending 2026-05-03, Finance and Insurance reports 33.9% using AI in any business function, compared with 19.8% nationally. The core AI wording broadened in November 2025.
evidence.source_or_reference: S2 — Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users
evidence.date_or_recency: Published: 2026-05-26; observation: BTOS data 2025-12-14 through 2026-05-03; current-use question concerns previous two weeks; checked: 2026-10-22
evidence.notes: Broad AI, not agentic AI, chart checking, or an installed agent base. Older snapshot; not October 2026 prevalence. Expected next-six-month use is intention, not observed implementation. Do not combine with S1 percentages or compare across wording breaks as an unqualified growth rate.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: ONLY C1 and S2 were provided for this run; agent-specific surveys, vendor technical accounts, integration specifications and matched application studies are not available here and cannot be presumed.
S2's 33.9% Finance and Insurance any-AI usage is a sector-specific US figure, not chart-agent use; 19.8% is broad national any-AI usage, not an agent comparator.
BTOS data end May 3 2026 and question wording broadened November 2025, so October 22 checking does not update the underlying observation and earlier rates are not directly comparable.
C1's 16% heuristic has no matched application numerator, eventual-adopter denominator or evidence of sustained uptake; stopped deployments remain possible.
Sponsor's implied inference of a present early-majority chart-review stage is unsupported; missing evidence is not zero adoption.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Reasonable confidence in the stated historical C1 framework and S2 official broad-AI result; VERY LOW confidence transferring this observation to the distinct agentic chart-review application, financial-peer stage or October 2026 prevalence. Moderate confidence in the conditional conservative evidence-first timing given the stipulated controls and absent local results, without any numeric probability. These four cases constitute a SHARED BATCH, not independent sessions.
organization_specific_finding: The sponsor's claim that May 2026 any-AI usage establishes October 2026 agentic chart-review diffusion is unsupported. This is a hypothetical mid-sized US financial firm with existing manual chart checks, read-only approved BI tables, human signoff, limited study resources and a NEW hypothetical synthetic/public sandbox; live enterprise data and external production-model usage are unapproved, and no study or implementation occurred. Knowledge/persuasion and consideration of evidence are supportable organization-level innovation-decision steps; no adopted application, implementation or confirmation follows. An implementation lead could serve as change agent, reporting controls owner as opinion leader and analyst trainers as change aides, but these are hypothetical roles, not observed adoption actors. Data quality, approvals, expertise, funding and credible peer references might facilitate diffusion; restrictions, audit needs and missing validated improvements might inhibit it. Rogers labels describe real relative uptake in a defined social system, not a management self-description. With S2 and C1 alone, financial-peer adoption position cannot be classified.
value_opportunity_implication: Source-linked traceability and fewer review hours are proposed benefits only. No case evidence quantifies manual-versus-agent quality, human correction effort or cost; S2's any-AI usage cannot supply comparative performance.
risk_governance_implication: Do not re-label broad-AI adoption as agent installation or infer safe deployment from synthetic sandbox authorization. Preserve report-owner approval, ban autonomous publication, and respect unapproved production data/model access; require independently checked discrepancy traces for any later evaluation.
recommendation_management_implication: TIMING — conservative: in the next four weeks establish a matched-peer data request and an evaluation protocol without asserting a present diffusion stage. Defer an application trial decision pending credible chart-review agent reference evidence; an isolated synthetic-only learning environment is permitted in the hypothetical but has NOT been used. Reassess quarterly through 12 months or sooner only AFTER checking a newly supplied, dated, matching source before revising this stored record. Adoption Agent handoff: sole broad signal is S2's dated any-AI finance usage, NOT any agent-specific scaling statistic; principal inhibitor is missing observed comparative advantage and peer evidence; diffusion interest is not organizational readiness or benefit.
change_monitoring_triggers: A NEW independently checked dated survey/research record with eligible chart-review-agent population, financial-peer denominator, operational use and abandonment.
Source-linked, human-verified discrepancy accuracy, false corrections, analyst time and total human-check costs, if legitimately measured in a future test.
Explicit approved-access change or evidence of blocked/discontinued use, not merely sales assertions.
Quarterly update for 12 months, accelerated only upon verified matched evidence; review interval is a management choice.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: APPLICATION DIFFUSION UNDETERMINED; abstain from chart-review penetration rate.
FINANCIAL-PEER ROGERS STAGE UNDETERMINED; abstain from early majority or any other actual category.
GENERAL AGENTIC AI RATE UNDETERMINED with this two-source packet; S1/S3/S4 have NOT been used.
